title: DEPTH=9 (same width as depth=10 winner, one fewer layer)
description: Changed DEPTH from 10 to 9 in train.py; model_dim stays 640 (5 heads) due to HEAD_DIM rounding, so this is a pure layer-count-at-fixed-width comparison against the depth=10 baseline.
reflection: val_bpb 0.998924, beating the depth=10 baseline (1.002530) by ~0.0036 and using less VRAM (61.9GB vs 66.5GB) since it's a strictly smaller model at the same width. This resolves the open question from round 1: at fixed width 640, depth=9 > depth=10 > depth=8(old baseline at different width) in this budget. Combined with depth=12 losing (confounded) and depth=11 crashing (same width as 12), the depth optimum at width=640 may actually be below 10 -- worth trying DEPTH=7 or 8 at width=640 (base_dim=448/512, rounds to 512, so width changes there -- careful, need base_dim>=513 to hit 640, i.e. depth>=9 with ASPECT_RATIO=64... actually depth=8 gives base_dim=512 which stays at width 512, not 640, so 9 is the smallest depth that reaches width 640). This is likely the new best result this round.
